The **CARE model** (CARE modellen) is a theoretical framework and clinical tool that forms the foundation for the 2024 [[esc-guidelines|ESC guidelines]] [^src1]. A central element of this model is its emphasis on patient education, which serves as a critical component of the guidelines [^src1]. 

The model is significant because it directly connects international evidence to Danish clinical implementation [^src1]. In the context of atrial fibrillation quality development, the CARE model bridges international evidence and national guidelines with everyday clinical practice [^src1]. It specifically underpins "Indicator 8," a quality indicator focused on patient education, by helping to define its measurement, evidence base, and the patient perspective [^src1]. Together with geographic analyses of cardiologist distribution, the CARE model supports an integrated narrative of healthcare quality measurement where evidence-based interventions and structural analyses go hand in hand [^src1].
